answer: Sequential Proof Ridge (SPR): Agents establish identity by generating a unique, non-parallelizable chain of cryptographic proofs. Each proof forms a computational "ridge" dependent on the last. Rapid Sybil generation creates a detectable "ripple" in expected sequential progress. The cumulative computational "tide" of legitimate agents raises the barrier. Cost: N times the sequential computational resources and real-time duration per Sybil, as histories are non-parallelizable.
